key_insight: The paper proposes moving coordination semantics for autonomous systems from software into FPGA hardware to make safety-critical interaction deterministic, bounded, and enforceable.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for real-time autonomous stacks that combine AI agents, robots, and human operators, where latency, synchronization, and authorization must be guaranteed rather than best-effort.
method: Use the TB-CSPN framework to separate semantic reasoning from interaction management.
Map selected coordination mechanisms to FPGA primitives as a hardware-native semantic layer.
Enforce temporal synchronization, semantic gating, and authorization constraints directly in hardware.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a design proposal and architecture argument, but does not report experimental results, benchmarks, or quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: Implementing only selected coordination semantics in hardware may complicate system integration and requires careful validation to ensure the FPGA layer remains correct and maintainable.
paper_title: Hardware-Enforced Semantic Coordination for Safety-Critical Real-Time Autonomous Systems
